record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: Is the property that every open ω-cover contains an open τ-subcover equivalent to the finite-selection property Sfin(Ω, T)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a topological space (typically a separable metrizable space, e.g., a set of real numbers). An open cover U of X is called an ω-cover if X is not a member of U and every finite subset of X is contained in some member of U. An open ω-cover U of X is called a τ-cover if for every two distinct points x,y of X, either {U ∈ U : x ∈ U, y ∉ U} is finite or {U ∈ U : y ∈ U, x ∉ U} is finite. Let Ω denote the collection of all open ω-covers of X and T the collection of all open τ-covers of X.

Consider the following two properties of X.

(a) The property ((Ω, T)): every open ω-cover of X contains a subfamily which is an open τ-cover of X.

(b) The selection principle S_fin(Ω, T): for every sequence (U_n : n ∈ ℕ) of open ω-covers of X, there exist finite sets F_n ⊆ U_n such that the union ⋃_{n ∈ ℕ} F_n is an open τ-cover of X.

Question: Are the properties ((Ω, T)) and S_fin(Ω, T) equivalent for all such spaces X?
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 preprint resolved the closely related problem ((Ω,T)) ≠ ((Ω,Γ)) by constructing a separating space, but it does not address the equivalence of ((Ω,T)) and S_fin(Ω,T). Standard surveys on selection principles list this as an open problem, and no published resolution was found in the available search results, so the current status could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: ((Ω|T)) ≠ ((Ω|Γ))
status_evidence.snippet: answers a question from the year 2003 by constructing a space satisfying (ΩT) but not (ΩΓ)
status_evidence.claim: A nearby problem comparing τ-cover-type selection properties was resolved in 2025, but this specific question between ((Ω,T)) and S_fin(Ω,T) is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Selection Principles and special sets of reals: Open problems
status_evidence.snippet: This paper gives a selection of major open problems involving selective properties, diagonalizations, and covering properties for sets of real numbers.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among open problems in selection principles.

status_evidence.title: Several comments about the combinatorics of tau-covers
status_evidence.snippet: the combinatorics of the selection hypotheses involving tau-covers is sensitive to the selection operator used
status_evidence.claim: τ-cover selection hypotheses are known to be sensitive to which selection operator is involved, supporting that the question is nontrivial.
